patterns.name: Completion + Prompt Engineering Baseline
patterns.intent: Use lightweight prompting for single-shot generation, classification, and formatting tasks.
anti_patterns: Using single-shot prompts for multi-turn agent workflows
Relying on prompt-only controls for high-risk tasks
implementation_outline: Construct concise instruction prompt
Call model once with deterministic settings
Compare prompt variants and capture outcomes

lecture_refs.why_relevant: Core completion workflows and prompt experiments.
Prompt refinements for classifiers and structured outputs.

patterns.name: Stateful Chat Agent
patterns.intent: Maintain turn history and system instructions for conversational behavior.
anti_patterns: Unbounded history growth without compaction
No role separation between system and user signals
implementation_outline: Initialize optional system prompt in history
Append user turn, call model, append outputs
Repeat until chat session ends

lecture_refs.why_relevant: Foundational chat loop with console and web options.
Stateful chat under adversarial prompting.

patterns.name: Jailbreak Testing + Prompt Guardrails
patterns.intent: Stress-test and harden agent behavior against adversarial inputs.
when_to_use: Prompt policy hardening and red-team exercises
anti_patterns: Evaluating only happy-path prompts
Prompt hardening without measurable regression checks
implementation_outline: Author constrained system prompts and boundaries
Run adversarial prompts/chats
Iterate instructions and verify failures are reduced

lecture_refs.why_relevant: Primary jailbreak examples and attack transcripts.
Security-oriented structured evaluation patterns.

patterns.name: Reasoning Workflow Prompts
patterns.intent: Use explicit reasoning scaffolds for multi-step thought and structured analysis.
anti_patterns: Assuming long reasoning text implies correctness
No verification after generated rationale
implementation_outline: Define stepwise reasoning instructions
Apply to target scenario with consistent template
Review output quality against expected constraints

lecture_refs.why_relevant: Reasoning prompt examples and comparative experiments.

patterns.name: RAG Ingestion + Retrieval + Grounded Answering
patterns.intent: Ground responses in retrieved corpus context with chunking and metadata.
anti_patterns: Ignoring metadata/chunk strategy
Presenting retrieved content as user-provided text
implementation_outline: Ingest corpus into vector store with chunk metadata
Retrieve relevant chunks/documents per query
Inject context with grounded response instructions

lecture_refs.why_relevant: Embedding-first RAG experimentation notebooks.
Operational RAG with Chroma ingestion and query routing.

patterns.name: Function Tool Calling (Local Tools)
patterns.intent: Allow model to invoke typed local functions in a response loop.
when_to_use: Deterministic helper functions enrich chat behavior
Need controlled side-effect execution with typed args
anti_patterns: Tool calls without input validation
No loop termination or timeout policy
implementation_outline: Register tools with JSON schema
Send tool definitions in model call
Execute function_call outputs and append function_call_output

lecture_refs.why_relevant: Core tool registry + schema generation loop.
Expanded tool safety and sandbox examples.

patterns.name: MCP Server Integration
patterns.intent: Integrate external capability servers through MCP.
when_to_use: Capabilities hosted outside the main app process
anti_patterns: No readiness/health checks for MCP servers
Hardcoded endpoints with no config strategy
implementation_outline: Define MCP server metadata and transport URL
Attach MCP tool entries to model tool list
Handle failures with explicit fallback behavior

lecture_refs.why_relevant: Client-side MCP tool usage examples.
Server-side FastMCP and deployment variants.

patterns.name: Multi-Agent YAML Orchestration
patterns.intent: Coordinate specialized sub-agents through declarative configs and tool handoffs.
when_to_use: Sequential or delegated multi-step agent tasks
anti_patterns: Overlapping agent responsibilities
No logging/attribution for agent contributions
implementation_outline: Define agents in YAML with tools/prompts
Expose sub-agents as tools to a main agent
Run loop with usage tracking and explicit termination

lecture_refs.why_relevant: Core run_agent orchestration and two-step chains.
Sub-agents wrapped as callable tools.

patterns.name: Agent Memory (Episodic + MemGPT-Style)
patterns.intent: Persist and retrieve durable memory across sessions while controlling context pressure.
when_to_use: Need durable user/profile memory and searchable history
anti_patterns: Unfiltered memory accumulation
No distinction between volatile context and archival memory
implementation_outline: Provide memory CRUD/search tools
Persist session/core/archival stores on disk
Inject memory summaries into active context with token budgeting

lecture_refs.why_relevant: Session-linked episodic memory tools and persistence.
Core/summary/fifo/archival memory management patterns.

patterns.name: LangGraph State Machine Orchestration
patterns.intent: Use explicit graph transitions, loops, and checkpointed state for deterministic orchestration.
when_to_use: Branching workflows with clear control flow
Resumable threaded state and human-in-the-loop loops
anti_patterns: Implicit control logic spread across prompts only
State mutations without typed contract
implementation_outline: Define typed state object
Build node graph with conditional edges
Persist checkpoints by thread/session ID

lecture_refs.why_relevant: Minimal but complete state graph demo with review loop.

patterns.name: Evaluation + Security Harnesses
patterns.intent: Measure output quality and safety regressions with explicit checks and helper tools.
when_to_use: Automated quality gate and regression monitoring
anti_patterns: Only manual spot checks
No objective metrics for quality claims
implementation_outline: Define measurable rubric checks
Run evaluator helper logic on outputs
Track failures and iterate prompts/tools

lecture_refs.why_relevant: Objective scoring helpers and app-level evaluation integration.
Human-factor framing for safe deployment decisions.

patterns.name: Governance and Human Factors Checkpoints
patterns.intent: Integrate representation, ethics, and human-impact controls into delivery lifecycle.
when_to_use: High-impact workflows with human decision effects
Need explicit policy/ethics review in design
anti_patterns: Safety and ethics only documented after implementation
No accountable ownership for approvals
implementation_outline: Define policy constraints and review criteria
Add human checkpoints for critical outputs
Record rationale and unresolved risks

lecture_refs.why_relevant: Content representation ethics analysis.
Human-factor and tool-calling ethics considerations.
